For the first time ever, ChatGPT's market share has dropped below 50%.

Sensor Tower's State of AI Report puts the current landscape at ChatGPT under 50%, Google's Gemini at 27.7%, and Claude at 10.3%. The remaining share is fragmenting across open-source and specialized models — and that fragmentation accelerated significantly this week.

Three major open-source models shipped in a single week. Moonshot AI released a trillion-parameter coding model with OpenAI-compatible APIs. Z.ai shipped GLM-5.2 under a fully permissive MIT license with a million-token context window. Poolside released Laguna M.1 under Apache 2.0 for agentic coding. All three are production-ready and available today.

At the same time, Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro remains stuck in preview as its availability promise slips, and OpenAI teased GPT-5.6 — a signal that even the market leaders feel compelled to announce ahead of delivery.

The practical implication for business leaders is straightforward: the era of defaulting to a single AI provider is over. The market now offers proprietary frontier models, open-weight alternatives with no licensing restrictions, and specialized vertical tools. A serious AI strategy accounts for all three tiers — with redundancy, clear evaluation criteria, and portability built in from day one.
